cards.text: Gideon is the man the LORD called to save Israel from Midian. Now the Midianites, the Amalekites and other people of the east gather together, cross the Jordan, and camp in the Valley of Jezreel. That's not a visit, friend. That's a MOVE-IN.

cards.question: With an enemy army camped in the valley, what comes upon Gideon?

cards.text: Gideon blows the ram's horn, and his clan, the Abiezrites, rally behind him. Then he sends out messengers to call even more men to arms.

cards.question: True or false: Gideon sends his messengers only to his own tribe, Manasseh.

cards.text: Gideon says to God, "If You are going to save Israel by my hand, as You have said," and then he lays out a test. He'll put a fleece of wool on the threshing floor overnight.

cards.question: What sign does Gideon ask God for with the fleece on the threshing floor?

answers.text: Dew only on the fleece and dry ground
Fire to burn up the fleece by morning
The fleece gone from the floor by dawn

cards.question: The next morning, Gideon squeezes the fleece and wrings out a ___ of water.

cards.text: A whole BOWLFUL. And Gideon says to God, "Do not be angry with me; let me speak one more time."

cards.question: True or false: For his second test, Gideon asks God to make the fleece dry and the ground covered with dew.

cards.text: That night God does it: only the fleece is dry, and dew covers the ground. I get it, friend, because the timer says done, I can SMELL done, and I STILL open that oven one more time.
Early in the morning, Gideon and his men camp beside the spring of Harod, with Midian's camp north of them in the valley. Then the LORD tells Gideon there's a problem with his army.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD tells Gideon his army is too small to beat Midian.
Why does the LORD say Gideon has too many men?

answers.text: So Israel won't say their own hand saved them
So Midian won't see them coming from far off
So the march to the valley will go faster

cards.text: So the LORD gives Gideon an announcement to make: "Whoever is fearful and trembling may turn back and leave Mount Gilead."

cards.question: After Gideon's announcement, ___ thousand men turn back.

cards.text: TWENTY-TWO THOUSAND head home, and ten thousand stay. That's like your boss saying anybody nervous can leave early, and the whole parking lot empties out.

cards.question: Then the LORD says, "There are still too many men," and has Gideon take the ten thousand down to the water. How will the LORD separate them there?

answers.text: By how each man drinks the water
By how fast each man can run
By how each man holds his sword

cards.question: Most of the men kneel down to drink. How many lap the water with their hands to their mouths?
The LORD tells Gideon that with the men who lapped, He will ___ him and deliver the Midianites into his hand.

cards.text: So Gideon sends everyone else home and keeps the three hundred, who take charge of the others' provisions and rams' horns. Three hundred men up here, and down below in the valley lies the camp of Midian.
That night the LORD tells Gideon, "Get up and go down against the camp, for I have delivered it into your hand." Three hundred guys against a whole army, and God talks like it's ALREADY DONE.

cards.question: The LORD gives Gideon another option. If Gideon is afraid to attack, what should he do?

answers.text: Take his servant and listen in on the camp
Ask for another sign with the fleece
Send in the three hundred without him

cards.text: So Gideon and his servant Purah sneak down to the outposts, where the camp fills the valley like a swarm of locusts, with camels as countless as the sand on the seashore. Right as Gideon arrives, a man is telling his friend about a dream.

cards.question: In the man's dream, what comes tumbling into the Midianite camp?

answers.text: A great stone from the hills
A wild ox from the fields

cards.text: It hits a tent so hard the tent overturns and collapses. Friend, my best cookie EVER couldn't knock over a napkin.

cards.question: The man's friend hears about the loaf flattening the tent. What does he say the dream means?

answers.text: God has given Midian to Gideon
Their camp will run out of water
A storm will hit the valley tonight

cards.question: True or false: When Gideon hears the dream and what it means, he bows in worship.

cards.text: Then he heads back to Israel's camp and says, "Get up, for the LORD has delivered the camp of Midian into your hand."
He divides the three hundred into three companies. Each man gets a ram's horn in one hand and a large jar in the other.

cards.question: Inside each man's large jar is a ___.
Before they move out, what does Gideon tell his three hundred men?

answers.text: Watch me and do as I do
Wait here until I come back
Run in as soon as it gets dark

cards.text: The plan: when Gideon's group blows their horns, everyone blows theirs and shouts. Gideon and his hundred men reach the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just after the changing of the guard.

All three companies blow their horns, smash their jars and hold up their torches, shouting, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!" I bet some guard JUST clocked in and hasn't even found his chair yet.

cards.question: True or false: Gideon's three hundred charge straight into the middle of the Midianite camp.
True or false: The entire Midianite army runs away, crying out as they go.
As the three hundred rams' horns sound, what does the LORD do inside the Midianite camp?

answers.text: Turns the men against one another
Sends hail down on their tents

cards.text: The army runs toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel-meholah. Men from Naphtali, Asher and all Manasseh chase them, and Gideon sends messengers through the hill country of Ephraim.

cards.question: Gideon tells the men of Ephraim to get ahead of the Midianites and seize the waters of the ___ as far as Beth-barah.
The men of Ephraim also capture the two princes of Midian, ___ and ___.

cards.text: They bring the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan. And that's where we pull this batch out for now, friend, because Gideon's story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: "Gideon is the man...", "Now the Midianites...", "That's not a visit, friend." and "That's a MOVE-IN." The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card says Gideon is the man the LORD called to save Israel from Midian. That fact comes from before the passage (Judges 6:14) and has no reference. The card cites only Judges 6:33.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question calls Manasseh Gideon's own tribe. That fact comes from outside the passage (Judges 6:15) and has no reference.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The setup from Judges 7:4 sits inside the question instead of on a story card: the LORD's quote "There are still too many men" and the move down to the water. No story card tells or cites 7:4.

rule.text: Story card: Papa Dorin's turn. He tells the next piece of the passage. The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: The question says the men are taken down to the water. Only the right answer mentions water, so the setup rules out both wrong answers and the right answer stands out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has three beats: Gideon and Purah go to the outposts, the camp fills the valley like locusts with countless camels, and a man is telling a dream.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The joke blends the modern comparison with the Bible setting. It puts a Midianite guard into a workplace image ("clocked in," "found his chair") instead of using one everyday image.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: This story card has three beats: the army flees toward Zererah, men from Naphtali, Asher and Manasseh chase them, and Gideon sends messengers to Ephraim.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.
